subject: Residency & transfer paths — where requests are processed (prospect Q&A)
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novushealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@novushealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Residency & transfer paths questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Novus is interested but our security team has a couple of gating questions before we move to a short pilot. Can you confirm at a high level: where do inference requests from our EU users get executed (regions and any temporary hops), and which subprocessors might see the data (cache, logging, monitoring)? We need to understand any potential cross-border transfers and whether Redwood can pin execution to an EU-only path for our pilot.

If you have a short checklist or a one-page diagram, that would help speed our internal review.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Senior Product Manager — Integrations
Novus Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & transfer paths questions

Hi Alex — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear ask.

Short answer: yes, we can route EU-origin requests to EU execution only for the pilot and provide detailed subprocessor visibility. High-level bullets below; attaching a concise map and the subprocessor inventory for more detail.

- EU pinning: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support region pinning (EU-only). For hosted API we offer an EU endpoint; requests routed to that endpoint are prioritized for EU execution but may transit to partner networks for orchestration — we include those transient hops in the evidence pack.
- Typical execution path: edge ingress (regional load balancer) -> routing plane (control plane metadata, no payload persisted) -> inference runtime (GPU worker in chosen region) -> optional KV/prefix cache (in-region or configured cache cluster) -> logging/telemetry pipeline (configurable retention; can be disabled for sensitive payloads).
- Subprocessors that may see metadata or telemetry: (1) cloud provider-managed logging services, (2) CDN/edge providers for ingress, (3) monitoring/metrics vendor for SLO telemetry. We provide a CSV listing versions, locations, and data scope (attached).

I'll let Marissa and Jonas drop in the attachment and a single-slide diagram showing the hops and which layers may cross borders. Also, please tell us if Novus requires contractual language around export controls or a specific in-country hosting guarantee — we can scope that into the pilot.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novushealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Residency details + attachments (redwood_residency_chart_v3.pdf)

Hi Alex — forwarding the single-slide map and our live subprocessor inventory. See the attached files and the quick notes below.

Attachment stubs: redwood_residency_chart_v3.pdf (PDF slide — execution hop diagram); subprocessor_inventory_20280315.csv (CSV — vendor, service, data scope, region, contract/contact).

Key clarifications:
- EU-hosted endpoint (api.eu.redwood.com): requests and payloads are routed to EU worker pools only. We operate pinned worker pools in Ireland and Frankfurt; customers can select a preferred EU cluster for the pilot.
- Transient hops: control-plane routing metadata (small headers, no payload) is handled out-of-region for coordination only; payloads for inference are not stored outside the chosen execution region unless you enable cross-region caching or choose multi-region replication.
- Caching & KV: by default set to in-region; if you enable global cache for latency we will flag that in the config and it's an explicit opt-in.
- Logging & telemetry: we retain structured telemetry (latency, errors) by default for 90 days; PII is scrubbed unless you opt to send identifiable tokens. We can reduce retention to 30 days for pilots and turn off verbose logging.
- Subprocessors: the CSV includes our CDN partner (EdgeFast Ltd. — ingress edges), metrics vendor (PulseOps — telemetry aggregation), and a managed GPU provider where we run dedicated clusters in specific regions. Each entry includes the country of operation and contract reference.

Compliance evidence: for pilot customers we provide an export of transaction-level routing logs (redacted) showing which worker processed each request and the region. We can also deliver a SOC-like inventory if needed for procurement.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodResidencyV3 (diagram), HubSpot: HS-4721.

Let me know if you'd like a short call with our compliance engineer (Jonas) to walk the team through the CSV.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Security — Redwood Inference

Alex
